records.name: Retrieval practice
records.definition: Recall information or perform a procedure from memory before looking at the source.
records.when_to_use: Use after initial learning; choose free recall, cued recall, explanation, problem solving or performance according to the target.
records.adaptation_rule: If retrieval repeatedly fails, provide a cue or brief restudy and retry; do not turn every attempt into a high-stakes test.
records.boundary: Recall success is evidence under the recorded conditions, not automatic mastery.

records.name: Distributed practice
records.definition: Spread meaningful practice across sessions rather than massing the same total practice into one sitting.
records.when_to_use: Select revisit timing from task complexity, intended retention horizon and observed success.
records.adaptation_rule: Shorten interval after failure; cautiously lengthen after repeated success.

records.name: Interleaving
records.definition: Mix related problem types so the learner must discriminate which method applies.
records.when_to_use: Introduce after basic methods are understood; mix confusable types and give feedback on selection cues.
records.adaptation_rule: Return to blocked guided practice if mixing only produces confusion or random guessing.
records.boundary: Interleaving is not random shuffling or a universal first step.

records.name: Worked examples
records.definition: Study a correct, fully explained solution to learn the structure of a new task.
records.when_to_use: Use for novices and high element-interactivity tasks; explain why each step is valid.
records.adaptation_rule: Fade prompts or remove steps as schemas develop.
records.boundary: Do not leave advanced learners trapped in redundant examples.

records.name: Faded guidance
records.definition: Gradually remove prompts, worked steps or scaffolds as performance stabilises.
records.when_to_use: Fade one support dimension at a time and test on parallel tasks.
records.adaptation_rule: Restore only the missing support when error patterns show a specific gap.
records.boundary: Support removal is based on evidence, not a timer.

records.name: Self-explanation
records.definition: Explain why a step, relation or decision makes sense.
records.when_to_use: Prompt causal links, assumptions, conditions and alternatives during examples.
records.adaptation_rule: If explanation becomes fluent but wrong, compare with evidence and test counterexamples.
records.boundary: Verbal fluency alone does not prove correctness.

records.name: Elaborative interrogation
records.definition: Ask why a fact or relationship is true and connect it to prior knowledge.
records.when_to_use: Use when prior knowledge is accurate enough to support connections.
records.adaptation_rule: If learner lacks the prerequisite, teach it first rather than demanding unsupported why answers.
records.boundary: Elaboration can reinforce misconceptions if the base knowledge is false.

records.name: Dual/multiple representation
records.definition: Connect words, diagrams, equations, demonstrations or physical models.
records.when_to_use: Use representations that reveal complementary structure; explicitly map corresponding elements.
records.adaptation_rule: Remove decorative or redundant representations that increase split attention.
records.boundary: More modalities are not automatically better.

records.name: Contrastive examples
records.definition: Compare similar cases that differ in one important feature.
records.when_to_use: Use to teach categories, method selection, misconceptions and boundary conditions.
records.adaptation_rule: Make the discriminating feature explicit after learner attempt.
records.boundary: Do not compare cases that differ in many irrelevant dimensions.

records.name: Error diagnosis
records.definition: Classify the earliest consequential error and its cause.
records.when_to_use: Keep the original attempt; locate misconception, cue-selection, procedural, arithmetic, attention or verification error.
records.adaptation_rule: Teach the cause and use a fresh parallel task.
records.boundary: Do not merely reveal the correct answer and repeat the same item.

records.name: Confidence calibration
records.definition: Record confidence before feedback and compare it with actual evidence over multiple observations.
records.when_to_use: Use low-stakes items with objective or defensible scoring; track sample size and confidence bands.
records.boundary: Never use confidence as a competence score or shame mechanism.

records.name: Goal decomposition
records.definition: Translate a broad ambition into observable outcome, evidence and next action.
records.when_to_use: Plan a specific target and success criteria before starting.
records.adaptation_rule: Reduce scope if target is vague or too large; increase challenge when stable.
records.boundary: Time spent is not the learning objective.

records.name: Attention and environment design
records.definition: Reduce avoidable interruption and make required materials accessible.
records.when_to_use: Prepare a bounded task, needed materials and a realistic stopping point.
records.adaptation_rule: Change environment or task size if repeated interruption or friction is observed.
records.boundary: Do not claim a universal attention-span number.

records.name: Deliberate component practice
records.definition: Target one weak, observable component with feedback and an appropriate challenge.
records.when_to_use: Use repeated high-quality attempts and gradually recombine components.
records.adaptation_rule: Stop or change task when fatigue, pain, overload or degrading technique appears.
records.boundary: Repetition count without quality criteria is not deliberate practice.

records.name: Variable practice and transfer
records.definition: Vary relevant conditions after basic performance is reliable.
records.when_to_use: Change one or two meaningful constraints at a time; include a transfer check.
records.adaptation_rule: Keep variation low when safety, technique or beginner control is not stable.
records.boundary: Difficulty should be desirable, not hazardous or arbitrary.

records.name: Feedback and feedforward
records.definition: Use evidence to identify current gap and a specific next action.
records.when_to_use: Feedback should be task/process/self-regulation focused, understandable and followed by another attempt.
records.adaptation_rule: Avoid overwhelming lists; prioritise one or two high-impact corrections.
records.boundary: Praise or criticism without information is not adequate feedback.

records.name: Reflective cycle
records.definition: Plan, perform/monitor, reflect and adapt the next attempt.
records.when_to_use: Apply to actual subject tasks, not only a detached reflection worksheet.
records.adaptation_rule: If reflection has no evidence, add an observable check before changing the plan.
records.boundary: Reflection is not self-blame or journaling for its own sake.

records.name: Sleep and recovery protection
records.definition: Protect adequate sleep and recovery as conditions supporting learning and safe practice.
records.when_to_use: Plan realistic sessions around school, family, movement and rest; use shorter fallback sessions when needed.
records.adaptation_rule: When tired, reduce complexity or stop; do not compensate with all-night study.
records.boundary: No study technique substitutes for sleep or professional support for persistent sleep problems.
